title: Total Fourier weight of a sign-valued function
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take values in $\{-1,1\}$. If $W_k[f]$ denotes the sum of the squares of the Fourier--Walsh coefficients over all subsets of $[n]$ of size $k$, then $\sum_{k=0}^{n} W_k[f]=1$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$
replaced:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $f(x)\in\{1,-1\}$ for every $x$;
for $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define
$\widehat f(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ and
$W_k(f)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat f(S)^2$ for $k\in\mathbb N$.
Then $\sum_{k=0}^n W_k(f)=1$.
